questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute percent error from measured and accepted values
questions.stem: A measurement gives 61.12 for an accepted value of 69.90. What is the percent error?

options.misconception: reports the fractional error but forgets to multiply by one hundred
divides by the measured value rather than the accepted value
keeps the signed difference instead of using its absolute value

questions.explanation: Percent error is the absolute difference between measured and accepted values divided by the accepted value, then multiplied by one hundred. The measured value can only serve as a denominator in a different quantity, the sign is removed by the absolute value, and the factor of one hundred converts a fraction into a percent.
questions.hint: Divide by the accepted value and take the magnitude.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: distinguish accuracy from precision using replicate data
questions.stem: Replicate titrations give volumes 25.07, 25.09, 25.05 mL, tightly grouped but all near 26.0 mL when the true value is 25.00 mL. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The results are both accurate and precise because the replicate values cluster together
options.misconception: assumes tight clustering proves accuracy without checking the true value

options.text: The results are precise but not accurate, because agreement among replicates does not guarantee closeness to the true value
The results are neither accurate nor precise because they deviate from one another
options.misconception: mistakes small random scatter for a total lack of precision

options.text: The results are accurate but not precise, since their mean sits near the accepted value
options.misconception: confuses repeatability with closeness to the true value

questions.explanation: Precision describes how closely repeated measurements agree with one another, while accuracy describes closeness to the accepted value. Here the spread is small so precision is good, but every value is biased high so accuracy is poor. A systematic offset can shift a precise set of results away from the truth.
questions.hint: Separate repeatability from closeness to truth.
